keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1901-1904: Cliopatria's first Commonwealth shape begins in 1905 but the page dates federation to 1 January 1901. The shape is the continent plus Tasmania (31,335 cells, equal to Natural Earth Australia within 0.4%), unchanged. Cliopatria 7.78 M km2 against the infobox land area 7,688,287 km2 (ratio 1.01).

keyframe_review.note: Right for the mainland and Tasmania, but it omits Papua (Australian from 1906) and the New Guinea mandate (1914/1920); Cliopatria draws these only in the Papua New Guinea row from 1946. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1906-1919: the Territory of Papua. 'The Territory of Papua was not formally constituted until 1 September 1906' (the letters patent of 18 March 1902 had placed British New Guinea 'under the authority of the Commonwealth of Australia'). The province split used for Papua is approximate; the page gives no boundary with the German north.

correction.text: mainland Australia and Tasmania, the Territory of Papua and the Mandated Territory of New Guinea (northeast New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago, Bougainville included)

'Australia assumed a mandate from the League of Nations for governing the Territory on 17 December 1920' (the Papua New Guinea page says 1921). Nauru and German Samoa were excluded from the mandate's title.

correction.text: the two Australian territories whole: Papua and New Guinea were Australian land in 1943 even where Japanese forces held it (contest events 1942-1945)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1943 shape adds 627 cells of Papua New Guinea (southeast New Guinea) and 16 cells outside it (8 in Indonesian western New Guinea, the rest coastal noise): it draws the Allied-held part of the two Australian territories, which stayed Australian territory throughout. The page: Japan invaded the Territory of New Guinea on 23 January 1942 and the Territory of Papua on 21 July 1942. Use the 1920 shape for 1943 with the Japanese-held land as the ledger's contest zone.

correction.text: the two Australian territories whole; western New Guinea stays Dutch (Netherlands East Indies)

keyframe_review.note: As 1943: the shape reaches -0.75 N and 135.5 E, so 50 of its 62 cells outside Papua New Guinea lie in Indonesian (then Dutch) western New Guinea, which the page calls 'part of the Netherlands East Indies', not in Australian territory. Use the 1920 shape.

correction.text: the two Australian territories whole; Dutch New Guinea excluded

keyframe_review.note: As 1943-1944: 292 of its 309 cells outside Papua New Guinea (west to 131.8 E) cover Indonesian (then Dutch) New Guinea, not Australian land; the Japanese were still blockaded in New Britain and elsewhere until the war ended (the page gives the campaign's end as 15 August 1945). Use the 1920 shape.

correction.text: mainland Australia and Tasmania plus the whole Territory of Papua and New Guinea (trust territory from 1946, administrative union 1 July 1949), to 15 September 1975; years 1946-1975 only

The page: the Territory of Papua and New Guinea was formed by the 'administrative union' of 1 July 1949 and independence set for 16 September 1975, so the whole of PNG belongs to Australia through 1975. Use the years 1946-1975 with all of PNG; from 1976 use the 1976 keyframe.

region.text: the six former colonies: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia, Tasmania

ledger.note: 1901: the six colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia. 'On 1 January 1901, federation of the colonies was achieved after a decade of planning, constitutional conventions and referendums'; 'From 1901, Australia was a self-governing dominion within the British Empire.' The name was formalised in the Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900 (UK).

region.text: the Territory of Papua, ex British New Guinea (province split approximate)

ledger.note: 1906: the Territory of Papua is constituted under Australia. 'On 18 March 1902, King Edward VII issued letters patent placing "our possession of British New Guinea under the authority of the Commonwealth of Australia"'; 'The Territory of Papua was not formally constituted until 1 September 1906' (Papua Act 1905). The Australia page says Australia 'took over the administration of the Territory of Papua (previously British New Guinea) in 1905'.

region.text: German New Guinea: northeast New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago (Bougainville included); province split approximate

ledger.note: 1914: Australian forces seize German New Guinea. 'The German administration surrendered German New Guinea on 17 September'; Rabaul was taken unopposed on 12 September 1914. Held under military occupation until the mandate of 1920.

1920: the occupation ends as the mandate begins. 'Australia assumed a mandate from the League of Nations for governing the Territory on 17 December 1920' (the terms 'were not received in Australia until April 1921'; the Papua New Guinea page dates the mandate to 1921).

region.text: the mandated Territory of New Guinea, with the Southern Highlands (german-new-guinea draws them in its loss and dissolve of December 1920)

ledger.note: 1920: Australia receives the League of Nations mandate for the Territory of New Guinea, 'German New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago' but not Nauru or German Samoa. Together with Papua this is the whole of modern Papua New Guinea. [fx-38 H39, 2026-11-01: the gain region now includes the Southern Highlands (88 cells). german-new-guinea ledger/15 (loss) and /17 (dissolve) hand Australia 922 and 930 cells, and this gain had 834 because the Southern Highlands were left out as undecided Papua/New Guinea land; the 1920 keyframe holds them, so the 88 cells were lost by Germany without a matching Australian gain. German New Guinea page: 'Germany lost all its colonial possessions, including German New Guinea' (Treaty of Versailles, 28 June 1919); infobox 17 December 1920 for the Australian mandate. The page and the Territory of Papua page never mention the Southern Highlands, so the Papua/New Guinea boundary is still unsourced.]
1927: the seat of government moves from Melbourne to Canberra. 'Melbourne served as the temporary capital from 1901 to 1927'; the ACT was formed in 1911 for the future capital.

region.text: the Antarctic sector between 45 E and 160 E south of 60 S, excluding Adelie Land between 136 E and 142 E

ledger.note: 1936: the Australian Antarctic Territory comes into force. 'The order-in-council came into effect on 24 August 1936' after the Australian Antarctic Territory Acceptance Act 1933; about 5,900,000 km2 between 45 E and 160 E south of 60 S, excluding Adelie Land (136-142 E). A claim 'accepted by just four nations' and frozen by the 1959 Antarctic Treaty (in force 23 June 1961); the gazetteer grid has no Antarctic cells, so it cannot be drawn as land.

region.text: the Territory of New Guinea, invaded from January 1942

ledger.note: 1942: Japan invades the Territory of New Guinea. 'On 23 January 1942, Japan invaded the Territory of New Guinea, after capturing Rabaul on New Britain that month'; Lae and Salamaua fell on 8 March 1942. The front then moves: Salamaua-Lae campaign 22 April to 16 September 1943, Huon Peninsula to 1 March 1944, New Britain campaign to 21 August 1945.

region.text: the Buna-Gona coast and the Kokoda Track (Northern province)

ledger.note: 1942: Japan invades the Territory of Papua. 'On 21 July 1942, Japan invaded the Territory of Papua and occupied Buna'; along the Kokoda Track the Japanese reached Ioribaiwa on 17 September 1942, about 30 km from Port Moresby, and the Australians began their counterdrive on 26 September 1942.

1943: the Japanese beachheads in Papua are cleared. 'Gona fell to Australian forces on 9 December 1942, Buna to the US 32nd Division on 2 January 1943, and Sanananda to Australian forces on 22 January 1943.'

region.text: the Territory of New Guinea, Japanese-held since 1942

ledger.note: 1945: the fighting ends. The New Guinea campaign page gives its end date as 15 August 1945; 'the Surrender of Japan to end the war on 2 September 1945' (Territory of New Guinea page). Japanese garrisons in New Britain, Bougainville and the north coast had been cut off and blockaded.

region.text: the Territory of Papua and New Guinea, then the independent state

ledger.note: 1975: Papua New Guinea becomes independent from Australia. The page sets '16 September 1975 as the date of independence' (the Territory of Papua and New Guinea pages say 15 September); self-government had come on 1 December 1973.

wars.name: Occupation of German New Guinea
wars.outcome: Rabaul taken unopposed on 12 September 1914 and the German administration surrendered on 17 September; Australia held the colony under occupation until the League of Nations mandate of 17 December 1920.
wars.note: A side-show of the First World War; the Territory of New Guinea page also says the German Solomon Islands (Bougainville) were occupied in 1914.

wars.name: New Guinea campaign

zones.text: Buna, Gona, Sanananda and the Kokoda Track in Papua

wars.outcome: Japanese invasion of the Territory of New Guinea (23 January 1942) and Papua (21 July 1942); Allied counter-offensives from September 1942; the campaign ended on 15 August 1945 and the territories stayed Australian.
wars.note: Western New Guinea was Dutch (Netherlands East Indies) and is not Australian land. The page does not date Finschhafen, Hollandia, Aitape, Sansapor or Wewak, so the zone is drawn whole until 1945.

certainty.note: The continent and Tasmania are bounded by sea and the federal borders were fixed by the 1901 Constitution; the Papua-New Guinea provincial split used here is approximate.
The front lines in New Guinea moved month by month; the Japanese-held land is drawn as one contested zone (page dates only some captures).
Island and coastal borders. The Antarctic claim lines (45 E and 160 E) are legal meridians, but the claim is recognised by four states only and is frozen by the 1961 Antarctic Treaty.

notes:
Written 2026-10-18 from six pages. Slugs of states other than Cliopatria rows are guesses at what the oc-02-x batch will name them: colony-of-new-south-wales, colony-of-victoria, colony-of-queensland, colony-of-south-australia, colony-of-western-australia, colony-of-tasmania (the six federating colonies, merge events 1901), british-new-guinea (counterpart of the 1906 Papua gain) and german-new-guinea (counterpart of the 1914-1920 occupation and the mandate).

Internal changes not entered as events because the Commonwealth's outline does not change: the Northern Territory passed from South Australia to the Commonwealth in 1911 ('The Northern Territory was transferred from South Australia to the Commonwealth in 1911') and the ACT was formed the same year.

Not settled (no page opened dates them): Norfolk Island, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, Ashmore and Cartier, the Coral Sea Islands, Heard and McDonald Islands; the Australia page names only Heard and McDonald and Norfolk as offshore territories and gives no years. A gap-filler should open 'Territories of Australia' or the individual island pages. Each is 1-5 H3 cells, so the map effect is small. The Antarctic Territory is entered but the grid has no Antarctic land cells, so it resolves to nothing; the region name 'Australian Antarctic Territory' goes to the gazetteer agent. Nauru, which the New Guinea mandate excluded, is not covered by any page opened.

Disagreements between pages: the mandate began 17 December 1920 (Territory of New Guinea) but the Papua New Guinea page says 9 or 19 May 1921; independence is 15 September (Territory of Papua and Territory of New Guinea pages) or 16 September 1975 (Papua New Guinea page, used). The Australia page says Australia took over Papua in 1905, the Territory of Papua page has letters patent in 1902 and constitution in 1906; the ledger uses 1906.

Cliopatria: the 1905 row begins four years after federation and omits Papua and New Guinea; the 1943-1945 shapes draw Allied-held New Guinea and, in 1944-1945, Dutch New Guinea (50 and 292 cells in Indonesian Papua); the 1946 shape carries 34 PNG cells (29 on Bougainville) to 2023, overlapping the Papua New Guinea row from 1976. Papua New Guinea's own 1946-1975 shape is declared wrong in its dossier (a territory, not a state) and replaced here by the whole of PNG as Australian land. The province split between Papua (Central, Gulf, Milne Bay, National Capital District, Northern, Western) and New Guinea (the rest of PNG without Southern Highlands) is mine: no page gives the boundary, and Southern Highlands is left out of both 1906-1919 shapes.

Neighbours to reconcile: empire-of-japan (jk-01) should carry the occupation of the Territory of New Guinea (1942-1945) as the mirror of this dossier's contest events; kingdom-of-great-britain and british-colonial-empire carry the loss of British New Guinea (1906) and of the Antarctic sector (1936); the Netherlands East Indies row (dutch-east-indies) holds western New Guinea, which Cliopatria's Australia 1944-1945 shapes wrongly include. Wikipedia pages budget: Australia plus four more, as the brief allows.
